answer_2.quote: We adopt the same metaevaluation metrics as the WMT 23 Metrics Shared Task, which defines a composite evaluation score based on four scenarios, each contributing equally (weight of 0.25) to the final meta score: -system-level pairwise accuracy; -system-level Pearson correlation; -segment-level Accuracy-t; -segment-level Pearson correlation

answer_3.quote: The emerging LLM-as-a-judge paradigm offers a promising alternative by leveraging large language models (LLMs) to directly assess or critique generated content.

answer_4.quote: You are an annotator for the quality of machine translation. Your task is to identify errors and assess the quality of the translation. Based on the source segment and translation, identify error types in the translation and classify them.
answer_4.guideline: The categories of errors are: accuracy (addition, mistranslation, omission, untranslated text), fluency (character encoding, grammar, inconsistency, punctuation, register, spelling), style (awkward), terminology (inappropriate for context, inconsistent use), non-translation, other, or no-error. Each error is classified as one of three categories: critical, major, and minor.
